message.content:
In Texas, tenants have a number of statutory rights designed to protect them from unfair treatment and to ensure they receive a safe, habitable living environment. Below is an overview of key tenant rights under Texas law (primarily the Texas Property Code). This is not legal advice; if you have a specific dispute, consult a qualified attorney. | Category | Key Rights | What It Means | |----------|------------|---------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | Landlords cannot keep deposits without proper documentation or justification. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, and pest control.
• Must provide adequate water, heat, and sanitation. | If the unit is unsafe or uninhabitable, tenants can withhold rent, repair & deduct, or terminate the lease. | | **Repair & Deduct** | • Tenants may repair a problem and deduct the cost from rent if landlord fails to act within 30 days of notice. | Must keep receipts and give written notice to landlord. | | **Notice Requirements** | • Landlord must give 30 days’ written notice before raising rent or terminating a month‑to‑month lease.
• For nonpayment, 3 days’ notice to cure or vacate. | Landlords cannot arbitrarily raise rent or evict without proper notice. | | **Eviction Process** | • Eviction requires a court order; landlords cannot forcibly remove tenants.
• Must file a complaint, serve a summons, and attend a hearing. | Tenants can contest eviction if notice was improper or if there are extenuating circumstances. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord must not interfere with tenant’s peaceful use of the premises. | Landlords cannot harass, enter without notice (except emergencies), or disturb tenants. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give at least 24 hours’ notice before entering, except in emergencies. | Landlords cannot enter without notice or for non‑essential reasons. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | Fair Housing Act applies to all housing transactions. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing for month‑to‑month agreements.
• Landlord cannot add new terms after the lease is signed without tenant’s consent. | Tenants can refuse to sign a lease that contains unreasonable or illegal clauses. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has no statewide rent control; however, local ordinances may apply in certain cities. | Check city ordinances for any rent limits or eviction protections. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide water, heat, and electricity unless otherwise specified. | Tenants can claim utilities are not provided or are inadequate. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlord must keep common areas clean and safe. | Tenants can request repairs or improvements in shared spaces. | | **Subletting** | • Landlord may prohibit subletting only if it is clearly stated in the lease. | Tenants can sublet if the lease allows or if landlord consents. | | **Lease Renewal** | • Landlord must provide notice of intent to renew or not. | Tenants can negotiate renewal terms. | ### Practical Steps If You’re Facing Issues 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of lease, notices, emails, photos of problems, and receipts for repairs. 2. **Give Written Notice** – If you need repairs, give the landlord written notice and keep a copy. 3. **Know Your Timeline** – Understand the 30‑day notice periods for rent increases or lease termination. 4. **Seek Mediation** – Many counties offer mediation services for landlord‑tenant disputes. 5. **File a Complaint** – If the landlord violates your rights, you can file a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office or the local housing authority. 6. **Legal Aid** – If you cannot afford an attorney, look for nonprofit legal aid organizations that specialize in tenant rights. ### Resources - **Texas Property Code** – Official statutes governing landlord‑tenant relationships. - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – Handles complaints about housing. - **Local Housing Authorities** – Provide information on local ordinances and assistance programs. - **Legal Aid Organizations** – e.g., Texas Legal Services Center, Lone Star Legal Aid. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is general in nature and does not constitute legal advice. For specific legal questions or disputes, consult a licensed attorney familiar with Texas landlord‑tenant law.
